aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer risk; the abstract does not provide stage, grade, metastatic, or other operational criteria for advanced disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Significant associations of dietary fiber intake (total, soluble, and insoluble) with advanced prostate cancer risk and prostate cancer-specific mortality in both arms were not observed (P > .05).
study_design: Secondary longitudinal cohort analysis of dietary fiber within the two arms of the PLCO randomized screening trial.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 49 476 participants (annual screening arm: 25 669 men; usual care arm: 23 807 men) aged 55 to 74 years were enrolled from the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Study between the years 1993 and 2001.
reason: The abstract analyzes both overall incident prostate cancer risk and advanced prostate cancer risk. Prostate cancer-specific mortality is also assessed in the trial cohort, but the clearest aggressive incidence endpoint is advanced prostate cancer risk. The reported HRs of 0.87 and 0.86 concern overall prostate cancer risk and must not be relabeled as aggressive.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Compared with the low tertile total fiber intake, high tertile total fiber intake in the annual screening arm was linked to reduced prostate cancer risk (adjusted hazard ratio 0.87; 95% CI, 0.76 to 0.99), and high-soluble fiber intake in the usual care arm had a similar association (adjusted hazard ratio 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.98) after adjusting for confounders.
estimate_classifications.reason: The 0.87 HR is explicitly for prostate cancer risk overall in the annual screening arm, not advanced prostate cancer.
